The Civil Defence, Correctional, Fire and Immigration Services Board has assured personnel of the Nigerian Correctional Service that promotion backlogs will not recur, following the promotion of 6,207 officers in the 2026 exercise. The Secretary of the board, retired Major General Abdulmalik Jibrin, gave the assurance at the decoration ceremony for the promoted officers in Abuja on Monday. Jibrin said accumulated promotion backlogs had previously affected personnel morale and contributed to the exit of some officers from the correctional service. He said President Bola Tinubu, following the intervention of the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, had approved the clearance of outstanding promotion backlogs. “I want to assure you that I will not allow that to happen again. Officers who give their best, and are tested and fulfil the requirements will certainly be given their due promotion,” he said. The Controller-General of Corrections, Sylvester Nwakuche, said the exercise involved 6,207 personnel, comprising 4,924 senior and 1,283 junior officers. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Nwakuche added that 743 Chief Correctional Assistants were converted to Inspectors of Corrections after completing the required conversion course, while 129 personnel were upgraded to the Inspector cadre upon acquiring relevant qualifications. He described promotion as recognition of service, competence and experience, urging the officers to justify their elevation through discipline, integrity and professionalism. “Promotion is not merely an administrative exercise or a change in designation. It is an important recognition of service, competence, experience and demonstrated capacity,” he said. 2027: Court of Appeal warns elections tribunal staff against bribery Police shake-up: IG redeploys 15 AIGs, CPs AU pushes joint action to recover stolen African assets Representing the Minister of Interior, the Permanent Secretary, Magdalene Ajani, said the promotion of more than 6,000 personnel in one exercise reflected the Federal Government’s commitment to personnel welfare and career progression. Tunji-Ojo described the exercise as a demonstration of ongoing reforms in the ministry, saying the reforms were repositioning the NCoS as a centre for transformation, reformation and rehabilitation rather than a mere facility for imprisoning offenders. He urged the newly promoted officers, particularly those assuming management positions, to demonstrate leadership, take initiatives and address challenges promptly. “You must play the managerial role of the positions you now occupy. You are not going to be waiting for directives while things are going bad because you will now be held responsible,” he said. The minister also urged the officers to share the service’s vision with their subordinates and ensure younger personnel were carried along in implementing reforms. Nwakuche further directed the officers to embrace the Performance Management System, saying future career progression would depend partly on performance records, competencies and measurable contributions to the service. He said the service mandate extended beyond secure custody to reformation, rehabilitation, reintegration and the administration of non-custodial measures. Also speaking, the Commandant-General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Prof. Abubakar Audi, urged the newly promoted officers to embrace discipline and mentorship. Audi particularly advised officers elevated to the rank of Controller of Corrections to prepare for greater command responsibilities and mentorship of younger personnel. The ceremony was attended by retired Controllers-General of Corrections, heads of other paramilitary agencies, traditional rulers, correctional service management officials, families and other dignitaries.
